To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) MLPA is a rapid and reliable method to screen for BRCA1 genomic alterations; 2) BRCA1 genomic deletion is frequent in Italian HBOC families; and 3) loss of heterozygosity at polymorphic markers in the BRCA 1 gene is a good predictor of BRCA1 deletion in HBOC families.
BRCA1 rearrangements account more frequently than previously reported in HBOC families and that MLPA is a rapid, reliable, and sensitive method for their detection.
the application of BRCA-1 MLPA to 22 uninformable HBOC families allowed the identification, in 5 families, of BRCA1 pathogenic mutations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of genomic rearrangements of the BRCA genes, which are responsible for the majority of the pathogenic mutations in breast/ovarian families.
the development of new molecular techniques to detect BRCA1 genomic alterations and with their clinical application to HBOC families.
the identification of BRCA1 rearrangements in Italian breast/ovarians families.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BRCA1 mutations, including genomic rearrangements, are the cause of breast and/or ovarian cancer in at least 50% of our families.
the BRCA1 genomic deletion is a major mutational event in northern Italian families, accounting for more than one-half (11/20) of all BRCA1 pathogenic mutations.
, in northern Italy, 40% of the BRCA 1 pathogenic mutations are genomic rearrangements, and that the MLPA methodology is the most suitable approach for their identification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the BRCA1- MLPA is a fast, reliable and cost-effective method for the detection of BRCA1 mutations.
the MLPA method has the advantage of being a rapid, sensitive, and inexpensive technique for the detection of large deletions and duplications of the BRCA gene.
BRCA1 rearrangements are not uncommon in Italian HBOC families, and that MLPA is a useful and rapid method for detecting them.
The main takeaway from our work is that

BRCA1- MLPA should be included in the molecular screening of Italian HBOC families, as well as in other populations, to improve the diagnostic yield and to provide a more complete genetic counseling to the affected families.
the application of MLPA in the analysis of uninformative HBOC families can increase the diagnostic yield of molecular testing for BRCA1/2 mutations.
BRCA1 rearrangements are frequent in Italian families, and that MLPA is a powerful and rapid method to screen for them.
